# tsk

> tsk is a terminal task board for you and your agents: one shared queue, a TUI for you, a CLI for them.

On macOS/Linux, install with `curl -fsSL https://gettsk.sh/install.sh | sh` or `brew install smarzban/tap/tsk`. On Windows 10/11 ARM64 or x86-64, run `irm https://www.gettsk.sh/install.ps1 | iex` in a PowerShell window (Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7); it selects the native architecture. Download the script first to use `-NoPathUpdate`, which leaves user PATH unchanged. Windows package-manager submissions and signing are not included yet.
If Herdr is on PATH, the installer asks to run `tsk setup herdr` on an interactive terminal; when agent skill roots are detected it also asks once to install the tsk skill. The install ends with a single `Done.` line pointing at the board (plus the Herdr board shortcut after an accepted Herdr setup) and one row per skipped ask (`tsk setup herdr`, `tsk setup`); a custom `TSK_INSTALL_DIR` skips the asks and says so. Homebrew prints the Herdr setup command as a caveat.
Herdr's board shortcut opens or focuses one board per workspace across its tabs, preserving its view and edits. Other workspaces stay untouched; boards share the same task store.
Details: https://gettsk.sh/docs/install.md
Inside Git, the repo root is the default project. Outside Git, tsk opens and captures on the desk while keeping the current directory available as a project. In `!p name`, `tsk add -p name`, and JSON plans, a bare project name must uniquely match a known project; a new project destination requires an existing absolute directory (`/…` or `~/…` on macOS/Linux, `C:\…` or `~\…` on Windows).
New tasks start with status `open` in the board's inbox, below picked `ready` tasks. Use the ready and open board commands to move them between groups, and `tsk list --open` or `--ready` to filter. The board checks GitHub releases at most daily and shows a dim `vX.Y.Z available, run tsk update` on the status row; set `TSK_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` to disable. Run `tsk update` to run the official installer for an installer-managed copy; on Windows a detached helper waits for the running executable to exit before replacing it. Existing Herdr registration and outdated installed agent skills are refreshed; when no agent skill is installed, an interactive update can offer the first-install skill setup. Homebrew copies print `brew update && brew upgrade tsk` instead.
Store format v11 adds `after` links; v10 added who and what on every event; v9 added review rounds; v8 added the undo step for a start that dispatched; v7 added blocks; v6 added task assignees, dispatch base branches, and dispatch records. An older store migrates on first save and keeps a `tsk.json.v<N>` backup such as `tsk.json.v5`; earlier migrations still run in order.
Agents: define launch profiles as `[agent.<name>]` tables in `<state dir>/config.toml` beside `tsk.json`, each a required argv `command`, an optional `prompt`, and optional string `env` values. Templates take `{number}`, `{title}`, `{notes}`, `{steps}`, `{worktree}`, `{branch}`, and `{base}` (the short base branch name); the rendered prompt is always appended as the last argument. Without its own prompt a profile sends a default that points the agent at `tsk guide`, the task notes, and the repo's AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, and asks it to work only on its branch, run the project's checks, open a pull request into the base without merging, then set the task to review or blocked. The first full board open seeds a commented starter file with examples for Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Grok, and any other terminal agent. Assign a task to an exact profile name with `!a name`, the board's assignee picker, the task page, palette **set assignee**, or `tsk add/edit --assignee` (clear with bare `!a` or `--unassign`); `tsk list --assignee name` filters.
Starting an assigned task dispatches it (the board start shortcut, palette set status: started, or `tsk status T<n> started`; there is no separate dispatch key): dispatch launches the assignee's profile in a new Git worktree and Herdr workspace (on Windows a preview), records the dispatch on the task, and sets it to started in one save. Undo right after reverts the status only and leaves the agent running. Starting a dispatched task whose agent still runs is a plain status change, as is a start by that agent itself; when the agent is gone the board asks before relaunching and the CLI refuses with `agent-gone` unless `--again`. `--no-dispatch` only sets the status. Outside Herdr or on a desk task an assigned start is plain and says `no launch: <reason>` instead of refusing. An unassigned task always starts plainly. Names follow the task: branch `tsk/t12-fix-login-timeout`, worktree `tsk-t12-fix-login-timeout`, workspace `T12 Fix login timeout`, agent `t12-<assignee>`. It starts from the task's base branch (`!b branch`, the task page's Base field or `⎇` footer, palette **set base**, or `tsk add/edit --base`), otherwise the repository's default branch (`origin/HEAD`), never the current checkout; bases must be existing branches, not tags or commits. tsk fetches the base first unless fetched in the last 60 seconds. A started task with a live dispatch shows `◉`. Starting a marked set where any task would launch opens one card listing what launches, what only starts, and what stays unstarted; relaunch is per task.
`N` tasks on the desk are human-only notices: four starter tasks on a first open, one `What's new in tsk` task after an upgrade. `tsk list` never shows them.
Peek footers read `@assignee · ⎇ <base> · #thread · project`, leaving out unset parts and a default base; the task-page footer always shows the base, such as `⎇ main (default)`.
Completing a task with a live dispatch on the board opens a cleanup card that shows whether its branch is merged into the recorded base; confirming completes the task at once and, in the background, closes the Herdr workspace, removes the worktree, and deletes the branch only when merged. A marked set gets one card and one undo step. Cleanup never removes a worktree with uncommitted changes and keeps any branch it cannot confirm is merged (not merged, squash-merged, fetch failed, base gone); the task keeps its dispatch record, marked cleaned. On Windows, cleanup may also stop with `files-in-use`, `path-too-long`, `removal-timed-out`, or `partly-removed`, keeping the live record.
Blocks: the block shortcut on a task that is not blocked opens a card for why, what it waits on (`you`, another task, or other text), and what it needs; `Enter` on an empty card blocks with no reason, and a marked set gets one card and one undo step. Rows with something to say carry a dim live line underneath (`└─`, wrapped, part of the row; the right edge stays empty): a block on you stays in NEEDS YOU with `■` and `@claude blocked on you · 2h` (or `blocked on you · 2h` when you set it); a review on you reads `@claude needs your review · 40m`; a block on another task or something else rides in IN MOTION with `□` and `waiting on T169` / `waiting on design team`, returning to NEEDS YOU (`T169 is done · unblock it · 1h`, or `T169 was deleted · unblock it`) once that task is done; a review handed elsewhere reads `@pi reviewing`. Notices have no live line. The peek replaces the live line: the same text, then why and `Decide: a · b` (or needs) for a block, or what was done and every check on one line for a review; no notes. The task page leads with a BLOCKED section above a rule: the row's live line on top, why and needs as plain text, options numbered `1`…`9`, replies as a thread (`claude · 3m` / `you · 1m` in one column, text beside), then a dim action line with only the keys that work right now, following the cursor (number keys to choose, reply, reply and unblock). You reply, pick an option with its number key (opens the reply box prefilled), or reply and unblock in one step (to ready, or for an assigned task a start that may dispatch); the start shortcut outside the box unblocks with nothing typed. `r` on a blocked board row opens the same reply box under the row (cursor only; `not blocked` elsewhere). When that unblock starts a task whose dispatched agent is still running, tsk sends it only the reply just saved (`[tsk T12 unblocked] …`, or the bare tag for an empty box), and only if the pane's live agent carries its dispatch name (`t12-claude`). The status row says `started · reply sent to @claude`, that the agent is waiting on a prompt or could not be reached, `reply not sent: @claude is not in its pane`, or `reply not sent: not in Herdr`; the task stays started and nothing relaunches. Save-only never sends. Leaving blocked closes the block; `tsk list --json` keeps it under `past_blocks`.
Reviews: the review shortcut on a task not in review opens a card for done, checks (one per line), next, and who it is on (`you`, an agent profile, or other text); `Enter` on an empty card sets review at once, a marked set gets one card and one undo step, and the shortcut on a task in review returns it to ready. Each review is a round. A review on you sits in NEEDS YOU with `▲` and the live line `@claude needs your review · 40m`; one on an agent or something else rides in IN MOTION with `△` and `@pi reviewing`. The task page leads with a REVIEW section (the live line on top, no round number; done and next as plain text; a `Check` list with `✓`/`✗`/`○` and passed ones folded into `N passed ▸`; the feedback thread; the action line: next, mark, feedback, send back, approve). The page opens on the first unmarked check; `Enter` (or a click) on a check cycles open → passed → failed → open in its own row without moving the cursor (passed checks fold the next time the page opens), `Enter` on the fold line shows or hides passed checks (folding takes in checks passed since). `r` opens the feedback box (on the page or under a review row): save-only keeps it in review; the start shortcut sends it back to started and, when the dispatched agent is confirmed running, sends `[tsk T12 sent back] <feedback> Failed checks: a; b` (status row `started · feedback sent to @claude`); the done shortcut approves (done, through the cleanup card for a live dispatch; never sends). The next review opens round N+1; closed rounds stay under `past_reviews` with `resolution` `sent_back` or `approved`.
Paper trail: below the steps, the task page lists who did what, newest first: status changes (`open → started · @claude 2m`), assignee and base changes, dispatch and relaunch (`dispatched tsk/t12-fix from origin/main @ 3333b79`), cleanup, archive, delete and restore, `title edited`/`notes edited` (never the text), steps (grouped: `3 steps checked`), and closed blocks and review rounds, which expand in place with `Enter` or a click. Agent changes name the profile from `TSK_AGENT`; everything else is `you`. It opens collapsed to a dim `PAPER TRAIL · 14 ▸` on every page open; `g`, `Enter` on the heading, or a click expands every entry (still dim) until another task's page opens. The task page footer no longer shows created and updated dates. Entries from a store before v10 show without who or what.
After: a task can run after other tasks (board-wide numbers, any project) and waits while any is not done. Set it with the task page's After field, palette **set after…** (task picker: type to filter, `Space` ticks several, **none** clears; loops refuse, `T202 already runs after T205`), quick-add `!w T202` (run after T202, repeatable), `tsk edit --after T202` / `--clear-after`, or `"after": [202]` in add plans. Palette **chain in order** makes each marked task run after the one marked before it, one undo. A waiting ready or open row's live line reads `after T202 (started), T205 (open)`; the peek and task-page footer show `after T202 · started` and the read-only `before T203, T204`. When the last prerequisite becomes done (review does not count), each waiting `ready` task starts through the normal start route in the done's save (an assigned one then dispatches); the status row says `T203 started · T202 done` and the paper trail `started · after T202`; a failed launch puts it back to ready and never blocks the done; undo of the done reverts the statuses only. Starting a waiting task asks first on the board; `tsk status T203 started` refuses `after-not-done` unless `--force`. Deleting a task drops it from every after list (undo restores the links); a ready task left waiting on nothing does not start (`T203 no longer waits (T202 deleted)`).
Multi-select marks a session-only set for status, archive, delete, assignee, base, and after changes. Leaving the mode, running an action, or changing the lens clears marks. Task details, editing, relaunch, and dispatch again remain cursor-only; starting a marked set where any task would launch opens one confirm card for the set. At 110 usable columns or wider, clicking a task opens or updates its details beside the board with board focus. Double-click opens it full screen. Narrow panes use click-to-peek.
On Projects Overview, clicking or moving the index selection opens the cursored project's preview beside the index at Split, then a live narrow project board at Rail, never a full-screen task. The right board names the selected project in its top row and owns its own selection and actions. Expanding quick-add there keeps the draft title in that header while Notes is active; Esc returns to the index.

On a project board `t` opens **Filter** with two tabs, `threads · @assignees` (`Tab` switches): a thread choice and an assignee choice (`@name`, including names whose profile was removed, or `unassigned`) combine, `all` clears one tab, and the control reads `#release @claude`. On Projects, `v` offers **Overview**, cross-project thread views, and `@name` views of one assignee's tasks across projects. Press `/` on any board tab to filter the rows it shows. Projects Overview matches project names and paths; task boards match every whitespace-separated query term against title, notes, steps, thread, assignee (`claude` or `@claude`), and `T` number. `Enter` pins the query and returns input to board keys, while `Esc` clears the input or a pinned query first. The done drawer is searched only while open, and changing tab, project, or Projects view clears search. In the wide Projects preview, `/` searches the right board when it has focus.

The quit shortcut exits from non-editor board surfaces, including task pages, Help, pickers, and the wide project preview. Text entry keeps its editing behavior; save recovery must be resolved first. Unsaved drafts block quitting, including drafts parked outside the focused project preview. Quit attempts preserve the pending save's failure message. Escape dismisses editors and overlays first, then collapses either wide split to its full-width board or projects index. Task drafts stay parked; unsaved work in a project preview prevents closing it. Escape then quits without confirmation at the full-board root on any tab, never switching tabs first. A narrow resize that hides the right column also exposes that root; parked drafts still block quitting. The browser demo releases keyboard focus at root instead of exiting. See the Keys guide for shortcuts.

## For agents

- `tsk guide` prints the workflow; `tsk setup` detects agents and can install the skill; `tsk setup <agent>` targets one agent
- The skill covers rules of engagement, board language, the exit contract, and workflows, and points at `tsk help <command>` for syntax; its `Refine a task` section shapes a rough task into a brief on the board (propose, then write)
- `tsk list T<n>` returns the complete task, including notes, steps, assignee, base, thread, dispatch, and its activity (the latest few paper-trail entries; with `--json`, every event newest first as `at`, `by`, `kind`, `detail`), in human-readable or JSON form
- `tsk status T<n> started [--again | --no-dispatch] [--force]` starts a task; an assigned task never dispatched launches its agent, so use `--no-dispatch` when you do the work yourself. A task that runs after unfinished tasks refuses with `after-not-done` unless `--force`; `tsk status T<n> done` starts the ready tasks it releases. `tsk edit T<n> --after T<m> [--after …]` sets the tasks it runs after (`--clear-after` empties; `invalid-after`, `after-loop`); `tsk list --json` rows carry `after` (`[{"task": 202, "done": false}]`) and a read-only `before`
- `tsk dispatch T<n>` launches an assigned project task's agent in Herdr; `--base <branch>` overrides one launch, `--again` relaunches a dispatched task with its recorded base. `tsk list T<n> --json` adds the `dispatch` record (`worktree`, `branch`, `base`, `base_commit`, `cleaned`, …)
- `tsk status T<n> blocked --why "…" [--needs "…"] [--option "…"]… [--on you|T<n>|"<text>"]` blocks with a question (again edits the same block); `tsk reply T<n> "…"` answers it (`not-blocked` without one); `--send` also delivers that reply (only it) to the task's running dispatched agent and prints `sent to @<agent>` or `not sent: <reason>`, leaving the task blocked. `tsk list T<n> --json` adds `block` (`why`, `needs`, `options`, `on`, `by`, `at`, `edited`, `replies`, `answered`) and `past_blocks`.
- `tsk status T<n> review --done "…" [--check "…"]… [--next "…"] [--on you|<agent>|"<text>"]` hands work back for review (again while in review edits the same round); `tsk reply` adds feedback to the open round. `tsk list T<n> --json` adds `review` (`round`, `done`, `checks` with `text` and `state` open|passed|failed, `next`, `on`, `by`, `at`, `edited`, `feedback`, `answered`) and `past_reviews` (adding `closed_at`, `closed_by`, `resolution`). Inside a dispatched agent, `TSK_AGENT` names the author
- `tsk clean T<n> [--json]` removes a dispatched worktree and its merged branch after review; `tsk status T<n> done --clean` completes and cleans in one step. Agents never clean the worktree they run in
- Guide: https://gettsk.sh/docs/agents.md
- CLI: https://gettsk.sh/docs/cli.md
- `tsk help [<command>]` prints the CLI or one command's syntax reference.
- `tsk --version` (or `tsk -V`) prints the installed version.

Storage, backups, and release-check settings: https://gettsk.sh/docs/storage.md
- Full docs: https://gettsk.sh/llms-full.txt
